newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols slide, active call selling.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols slide, active call selling.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options declined Wednesday as the underlying futures worked their way back from an early selloff to end slightly lower on the day, dealers said.
Bond market participants liquidated calls as futures spent the bulk of the session retracing the morning selloff, which was triggered by stronger than forecast manufacturing data, floor traders said.
Industrial production rose 0.9 percent in March, and the capacity utilization rate climbed to 84.1 percent, a two-year high.

Implied volatility for June bond options was 8.30 percent late in the session, down from Tuesday's settlement of 8.45 percent. Volatility for May options, which go off the board Friday, was 6.9 percent, compared with 7.4 the previous day.

Among the day's notable transactions, a U.S. banking firm sold 2,000 May 108 calls, a Wall Street dealer firm sold 1,000 June 110 calls, and a U.S. brokerage firm sold 500 May 108 calls. Buying interest in June 105 puts also was seen.
Trading patterns suggested a shift in sentiment from the previous session, which saw good interest in May call purchases.

Eurodollar options volatility was about unchanged from Tuesday, with September at 10.0 percent and December at 12.0 percent late in the session. Short-dated mid-curve options, which expire in 1997 but are priced from 1998 futures, were also steady, quoted at 15.8 percent in both June and September.
A U.S. brokerage firm purchased 1,000 September 93.70 calls, another firm sold 1,000 March 93.25 straddles and a third house bought 2,000 short-dated May 93.00 puts.
